rows.grounds: compound: lalāṭa (forehead) + varṇa (letter) + rāśi (mass) + stha (situated); describes the locus of the practice
numerical measure indicating the required count of repetitions
absolutive indicating completion of the prescribed act
compound vocative: sura (god) + arcita (worshipped); address to the qualified recipient

items.question: What repeated practice at the forehead-letter locus fulfills the guarded Kaula transmission?
premises: The prescribed act is situated in the forehead's mass of letters.
The act must be performed a hundred-thousand times.
The instruction addresses one honored by the gods.
items.inference: A hundred-thousandfold performance at the forehead-letter locus completes the guarded Kaula practice.
uncertainties: Whether lakṣaṃ specifies mantra repetitions, offerings, or another counted act is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: O one worshipped by the gods, having performed a hundred thousand times what is situated in the mass of letters on the forehead.
